evidence_refs: HEAD src/httpx/_server.py:111-113 removes the try/except and calls sleep(1) in an infinite loop.
BASE src/httpx/_server.py:103-108 caught KeyboardInterrupt and broke from HTTPServer.wait().
HEAD src/httpx/_server.py:128-137 advertises CTRL+C as the quit mechanism and has run() call server.wait() directly.
resolved_finding.technical_rationale: The base implementation absorbed KeyboardInterrupt and returned from HTTPServer.wait(), whereas the head implementation allows it to propagate through wait() and run(). The surrounding context manager still performs cleanup during unwinding, but callers and command-line users observe changed termination behavior, potentially including an uncaught KeyboardInterrupt traceback. The frozen diff directly establishes this regression. Annotator B's base line range is inaccurate, but its described code is present at base lines 103-108 and the error does not undermine the finding.
resolved_finding.comment_usefulness_rationale: A developer-facing comment is useful and actionable because retaining the prior KeyboardInterrupt guard would preserve the advertised synchronous CTRL+C shutdown behavior independently of the parser-readiness change.

pairings.rationale: Both annotations identify the same removed KeyboardInterrupt handler, the same affected method and head lines, the same low severity, and the same actionable restoration. Their taxonomy labels differ only in specificity: “error-handling-regression” is a subtype-style formulation of “error-handling,” so there is substantive taxonomy agreement.

summary: The two findings form one deterministic pair and agree on every adjudication dimension. Repository evidence confirms a low-severity error-handling regression in the synchronous CTRL+C shutdown path; no additional context is required.
